s: nach- + arbeiten (“to work”) → nacharbeiten (“to rework, touch up”)
nach- + klingen (“to sound, make a sound”) → nachklingen (“to echo, linger”)
indicates following or pursuit of someone or something
nach- + gehen (“to walk”) → nachgehen (“to follow, pursue”)
nach- + fahren (“to drive”) → nachfahren (“to follow someone [by car]”)
nach- + füllen (“to fill up”) → nachfüllen (“to refill”)
indicates repetition or succession: to check something
nach- + zählen (“to count”) → nachzählen (“to count again, double-check an amount”)
indicates repetition or succession: to improve something
nach- + helfen (“to help”) → nachhelfen (“to give extra help; give private lessons”)
indicates the exact copying of something
nach- + machen (“to do”) → nachmachen (“to copy, imitate”)
nach-.et: Formed from the preposition nach (“past, after”).
